newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: RESEARCH ALERT-ICTSI rated buy on Subic bid.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-ICTSI rated buy on Subic bid.

text.p: International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTSI) was rated a buy on Friday by Angping Securities after President Fidel Ramos ordered a re-bidding of the Subic Bay container port project.

ICTSI had offered the highest royalty of $58 per tewnty-foot equivalent unit (TEU) during last year's bidding but it was rejected by the Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority (SBMA) on the grounds that it would violate a law forbidding monopolies in the port industy.
"Subic Port is back on ICTSI's list of prospective ports to develop, manage and operate here in the Philippines," Angping Securities analyst Alexis Cabel said in an advisory to clients.
"Though ICTSI is fairly valued at this point, ICTSI is still a buy. The chance of bagging Subic gives the issue a speculative flavour on top of its strong fundamentals," he said.
ICTSI is currently the operator of the Manila International Container Terminal which handles 70 percent of container traffic in the country.

Although the Philippine Ports Authority's (PPA) anti-monopoly policy is a major obstacle to ICTSI's expansion in the country, the Subic port is exempted from this because it is under the jurisdiction of the SBMA, Cabel said.

He added the winning operator of Subic will be able to enjoy extra savings and incentives. Some of these include a five-year exclusivity contract on the port; lower costs since reclamation and dredging will be done by the SBMA; and tax provisions of 20 to 25 percent versus the normal corporate income tax of 35 percent.
